verdict:
Verified against real source, not taken on trust. Claims (a), (b), (d), (f) and (g) HOLD — I could not refute them, and I strengthened the evidence for each. Claim (c) holds in its conclusion (`babele.init` is the right hook) but rests on three false supporting statements, now corrected. Claim (e) holds completely: every id, version and compatibility range in the three module.json files matches the installed manifests byte for byte. The glossary is the strongest artefact of the set — 346 terms, zero bare-Chinese-frequency adoptions, subtitle corpus correctly weighted as one vote, 32 pending terms with none leaked — but it carries one corrupted candidate, two entries glossed against its own proper-noun rule, and three wrong actor.mjs anchors in the lockstep block. 12 refutations, 9 missed items, 17 fixes applied; all 27 CI run-blocks pass `bash -n`, all three module.json + four glossary JSONs re-validated, and every glossary invariant re-asserted after editing.

VERIFIED, NOT REFUTED (each re-derived): (a) `#filterLanguagePaths` at localization.mjs:331-339 — the README's quoted block is byte-identical to source; `checkModule = !l.module || game.modules.get(l.module)?.active` at :335; the field genuinely survives DataModel validation (base-package.mjs:373 declares `module` with `validate: BasePackage.validateId`), and validateId's `/^[A-Za-z0-9-_]+$/` (:592) accepts `motion_tracker`'s underscore. All four gated ids are installed. (b) push order core :288-290 → system :293-297 → modules :300-305 → world :308-312, merged in push order at :316-319; later-wins is real because mergeObject defaults `overwrite=true` (helpers.mjs:1126) and `_mergeUpdate` assigns at :1219-1224. It is a genuine override, not a sole-source situation: systems/alienrpg/system.json really does declare `{"lang":"cn","path":"lang/cn.json"}`. (d) modules 2 and 3 contain no registerMapping call, and that is correct — document-mappings.js:351-354 CONCATENATES `_variants`, so a triple registration would triple every variant. (f) two independent gates gate compendium/en: the `-x` pattern and the `^compendium/en/` grep assertion. (g) `git check-ignore -v` reports not-ignored for the findings and glossary; all 11 findings show as `??`; the fvtt repo root has no .gitignore at all and the only three that exist live inside the nested module repos, which cannot reach `7-其他内容/`. (e) Foundry 14.366.0, alienrpg 4.1.13, babele 2.9.1, alien-evolved-{starterset,corerules} 1.0.2, alien-mu-th-ur 2.0.0, motion_tracker 1.5.5, token-action-hud-alien 1.3.0 — all match; `_source.json` pack collections match the manifests; the README's `base-package.mjs:455-456` reading of `maximum` is exact. Glossary: all 12 T-EXACT values byte-equal lang/cn.json ALIENRPG.Skill*, all 28 T-FROZEN byte-equal their English key, all 101 bilingual_name strings satisfy the contract, and I re-ran term_gate.py on three of the file's own corrections (Ripley 蕾普丽 75, Quarantine 检疫 4 / 隔离 2, Bug Hunt 2) — all three held exactly.

refuted_claims.claim: scripts/alienrpg-hardcoded-cn.mjs:71-74 — "i18nInit 由 Localization#initialize 在 `init` 钩子**之前**触发".
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Exactly backwards. `init` fires FIRST; `i18nInit` fires inside i18n.initialize() eleven lines later. The code still works (settings/keybinding labels localize at render time) but the stated reason is false, and the inverted model would lead someone to 'simplify' the patcher into the `init` hook, where game.i18n.translations does not yet exist.
refuted_claims.evidence: C:/Program Files/Foundry Virtual Tabletop/resources/app/client/game.mjs, `Game#initialize()` at :648-676 — line 652 `Hooks.callAll("init");`, line 660 `this.registerSettings();`, line 663 `await this.i18n.initialize();`. i18nInit itself is client/helpers/localization.mjs:104 `Hooks.callAll("i18nInit");`, reached only from inside that :663 call.

refuted_claims.claim: All three register.js files — "所以放 `ready` / `setup` 不是「晚一点」，是**直接报错**" (registering outside babele.init is a direct error).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: `#assertConfigurable` returns early when no session exists, and the session is only built in Babele's own `ready` listener. So a `setup`-time registration never throws and works fine, and a `ready`-time one throws or not depending on hook order. Treating the exception as a guardrail is unsafe: it fires in roughly half the cases. The real justification for babele.init — Babele dispatches it itself, immediately after building game.babele, so there is neither an object-existence nor a session-timing race — is sound and now stated on its own.
refuted_claims.evidence: modules/babele/script/babele.js:984-994 `#assertConfigurable(operation) { if (!this.#session) { return; } throw new Error(...) }`; `#session` is assigned only via `init()` :417-438 → `#replaceSession()` :859-903 → `#installSession()`, and `game.babele.init()` is called from Babele's own `Hooks.once('ready')` at :36-42. Constructor sets `this.#session = null` at :143.

refuted_claims.claim: All three register.js files — the registerMapping docstring is at "babele.js:285-294".

Runtime sessions reject late mapping"), so the quoted range does not contain the text quoted next to it. The real block is 281-294: docstring 281-290, method body 291-294. The quotation also silently dropped the third sentence, which is the one that explains the late-registration rejection.
refuted_claims.evidence: modules/babele/script/babele.js:281 `/**`, :282 `* Register one global document mapping layer.`, :284-286 `* Registered mappings enrich or override the built-in defaults for every / * session built after bootstrap. Runtime sessions reject late mapping / * registration to keep configuration and loaded data coherent.`, :291 `registerMapping(mapping) {`, :294 `}`.

missed_items.what: Registering `compendium/cn` with Babele silently opens a SECOND mapping channel that outranks the hub's registerMapping layer. The same directory is handed to Babele as both translationDirectories and mappingDirectories, and Babele decides which a `.json` is purely by FILENAME: `mappings.json` and `mapping.json` are reserved words in that directory. Two failure modes, both silent: a translation file named `mappings.json` is eaten as a mapping and translates nothing without error; a mapping file placed there lands in `loadedMappings`, which `#rebuild` merges AFTER `registeredMappings` and therefore overrides the hub's global layer.
missed_items.where: modules/babele/script/translation/translation-source-registry.js:61-62 (same dir used for both); translation-source.js:14-15 `MAPPING_FILENAME = "mappings.json"` / `LEGACY_MAPPING_FILENAME = "mapping.json"`, :115-126 `#isMappingFile` / `#matchesKind`; mapping/document-mappings.js:267-281 `#rebuild()` order builtIn → registered → loaded. Affects all three modules' register.js and all three compendium/cn dirs.
missed_items.why_matters: The project's whole mapping story is 'exactly one global layer, registered by the hub'. A single file dropped into compendium/cn with one of two very natural names would either quietly beat that layer or quietly not translate. Neither logs anything. Nothing in the three skeletons mentioned the reserved names.

missed_items.what: Module 1's release workflow had no 'something to ship' gate, while modules 2 and 3 both do. In its current skeleton state module 1 would pass every existing check and cut a real release that does nothing: lang/cn.json is 3 bytes (`{}`), all four lang/plugins/*.json are 3 bytes, and compendium/cn holds only .gitkeep.
missed_items.where: 1-系统汉化插件/.github/workflows/release.yml — the step list went straight from 'Verify every declared file actually exists' to 'Build module.zip'. Compare 2-新手包汉化插件/.github/workflows/release.yml, which has 'Verify there is actually something to ship' gating on a non-empty compendium/cn.
missed_items.why_matters: The existing 'declared file exists' check passes on an empty JSON file, so the one asymmetry between the three repos is exactly the one that lets a no-op v0.1.0 reach users. The failure presents to users as 'installed it, nothing happened', with no console error to diagnose.

missed_items.what: A module lang file can OVERWRITE a system key but can never DELETE one. mergeObject defaults to `applyOperators=false`, so the `-=key` deletion syntax is inert, and `performDeletions` is deprecated as of v14. The correct handling for a system key that must fall back to English (e.g. ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries, which the system's cn.json holds as JSON null) is to write NOTHING for it and let localize() fall through to `_fallback`.
missed_items.where: common/utils/helpers.mjs:1127 (`applyOperators=false` default), :1132-1138 (performDeletions deprecation warning, since 14 until 16); client/helpers/localization.mjs:441 (`translation = foundry.utils.getProperty(this._fallback, stringId);`). The 1-系统汉化插件/README.md override section stated 'later wins' without stating this limit.
missed_items.why_matters: The system's cn.json carries dead pre-v11 orphan keys and at least one JSON-null value. A maintainer who assumes 'our file overrides theirs' will try to delete rather than shadow, get no error, and ship a broken RollTable lookup.

missed_items.what: Both runtime patchers pre-register Handlebars partials with bare `Handlebars.compile(source)`, while Foundry's own loader compiles with `{preventIndent: true}`. A partial compiled without it re-indents its output when inlined by `{{> ...}}`.
missed_items.where: 1-系统汉化插件/scripts/alienrpg-hardcoded-cn.mjs (the init hook's registerPartial loop) and scripts/plugins-hardcoded-cn.mjs (same); core's reference behaviour is client/applications/handlebars.mjs:41 `const compiled = Handlebars.compile(resp.html, {preventIndent: true});`.
missed_items.why_matters: The named targets for channel B are `terminal` and `motion-tracker-multideck` — ASCII-art / monospace UIs whose box drawing is destroyed by leading whitespace. The bug would only appear on the modules the channel exists for, and only after someone fills the currently-empty table.

missed_items.where: glossary_alien.provenance.json terms: LV-426 (franchise-place), LV-223 (franchise-place), MU/TH/UR (franchise-computer), USCSS (franchise-ship). The 24 entries in the frozen-* categories are the mechanics-critical set; 28 carry the tier.
